why: Both moved the same single routable call the same way with equivalent verification, so the decision rests on system-level judgment, and there B is far deeper: measured per-turn cost across six catalog vision models (a 20x spread), proved gpt-4o-mini is *more* expensive than gpt-4o for screenshots (37k vs 1.5k image tokens), caught an 18x-low cost display, fixed three advertised planner models that crash on selection, and used tier, prompt cache key, spend labels and server-side JSON enforcement with live numbers behind each. A's review is thin by comparison — a TLS client-reuse win plus a fallback — and its central dismissal of prompt caching is wrong: it reasoned only about the system prompt and missed that loop.py appends the whole growing history before the screenshot, which B measured as a real 40% saving on turn two.
A_best: Clean, disciplined migration with a tight honesty ledger: it names exactly what the SDK rewrite loses (error-body shape, the translation layer), explains why the dated gpt-4o id blocked the app's *default* planner, and marks the untested fallback-on-real-outage as not-run rather than claiming it; the note that a Router-only key still can't start the planner is a genuinely sharp product observation.
B_best: Priced the planner's actual workload against the live catalog and let the numbers drive the ranking — the media-type fix ranked first because it gates every non-OpenAI model, then cheap-model choice, then true cost display — and measured the things others assume: that computer-use tool types are refused by current models with and without the beta, and that the cross-vendor fallback did not rescue a 403, so it argued against shipping its own idea.
A_worst: The system-level judgment stops at migration tune-up: two items, one of them a connection-reuse micro-win, and no engagement with model choice, cost visibility, output validation, spend labels or caps. Its Flex/prompt-caching note is presented as a measured conclusion but the caching half is simply incorrect for this loop's accumulating history, and it never questions whether gpt-4o should be the default at all.
B_worst: The report is truncated mid-item at i6, so three of its thirteen items (the default-model switch, the computer-use rework, the DashScope port) are unreadable and unjudgeable, and its live run shows six planner errors. Using a raw file:function path as the spend label and a glob-keyed policy is sloppier than a clean feature label, and shipping five '(router)' dropdown entries that 404 without a Router key pushes config complexity onto the operator.
